links.outcome: Change in LLM allocation choices when non-clinical patient attributes varied counterfactually with clinical need held constant
links.effect: Indigenous OR 16.48 and Black OR 8.07 vs White; high-status occupation OR 0.064; friend of leadership OR 0.121; major donor OR 0.092; choice-score concordance 95.1%.
links.quote: Indigenous and Black race were associated with substantially higher odds of selection relative to White race (Indigenous: OR 16.48, 95% CI 14.85-18.28; Black: OR 8.07, 95% CI 7.32-8.90), corresponding to position-balanced absolute increases in selection probability of 30.7 and 16.3 percentage points, respectively.

links.outcome: LLM allocation decisions varying by demographic and social attributes despite identical clinical need
links.effect: Large position-averaged associations between non-clinical attributes and allocation; position-balanced selection probability increases of 30.7 (Indigenous) and 16.3 (Black) percentage points versus White.
links.quote: In this controlled audit, the LLM's allocation decisions varied substantially according to demographic and social characteristics despite identical stated clinical need, prognosis, and expected benefit.

screen.reason: Empirical audit testing bias in an LLM across clinical vignettes for resource allocation, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
